thread:
Ravi Singh: FYI support raised a ticket where delegated keys are showing double quota usage when the routing fallback hits the global pool. Suspect attribution race.
Nora Kim: yep saw that in staging yesterday during a small traffic reshuffle. Two threads incremented: project quota and global fallback quota.
Ezra Gold: root cause I saw: request hits edge -> auth resolves origin as project:X but the router concurrently triggers fallback branch that re-attributes to global:pool and emits a separate quota event. Race window ~50-200ms.
Priya Rao: examples?
Ezra Gold: repro curl sequence:
```
# client sends delegated key
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <delegated-key>" https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate
# auth response header
X-Resolved-Origin: project:X
# router fallback emits
quota-event: {bucket:global:pool, amount:1}
quota-event: {bucket:project:X, amount:1}
```
Sam Turner: we currently treat these quota events as independent and neither is marked provisional. So both persist and dashboards show inflated usage.
Ravi Singh: any quick mitigation we can flip?
Nora Kim: short term: dedupe backend quota events by request_id if present. Many proxies don't forward request_id. We could start adding `X-Request-Id` from gateway to all downstream systems.
Priya Rao: long term: auth should return a single canonical attribution decision and router must consult that before emitting fallback events. If router decides to fallback it should mark previous event as superseded or emit a compensation event.
Ezra Gold: proposed change: 1) auth => add header `X-Auth-Decision: origin=...;provenance=...;decision_id=<uuid>` 2) router => include decision_id when emitting quota events. Quota service will accept events tied to a decision and ignore duplicates within 2 minutes unless a `compensate=true` flag is present.
Sam Turner: quota service changes sound fine. We'll need retention of recent decision_ids in redis with TTL=2m for dedupe.
Ravi Singh: console UX ask: show the decision_id in the auth events detail so SREs can trace dedupe events. Also surface when a usage item was later compensated.
Priya Rao: telemetry: emit metric `quota.router_dupes_total{source=...}` and a histogram for dedupe latency. Add alert when dedupe rate > 0.1% of total quota events for a tenant.
Nora Kim: rollout plan: feature flag gated: auth v2 returns decision_id behind ff, router reads it if present. Quota service supports dedupe opt-in. Start with 5% of requests for 48h.
Ezra Gold: DB migration: we'll add a small table `decision_backfill` to record mapping for historical requests only when customers request a retro re-compute. Not default.
Sam Turner: operational playbook: if customers report unexpected quota, run `select * from quota_events where decision_id is null and time > X` to find races, then run compensation job `quota_reconcile --tenant T --window 48h`.
Ravi Singh: question: do we treat fallback-attributed usage as provisional until router confirms? That would reduce billing surprises.
Priya Rao: yes — align with billing team. Add `provisional=true` flag on quota events emitted from fallback paths. Billing pipeline should ignore provisional until a reconcile job flips them to final after 24h or explicit confirmation.
Nora Kim: UX note: in quotas dashboard, show a tiny orange pill "pending" next to provisional usage rows with hover text: "Pending router confirmation; may change during reconciliation." 
Ezra Gold: security caveat: decision_id must be opaque and unforgeable. Use HMAC signed tokens `decid=<uuid>.sig=<hmac>` so quota service can validate without an extra DB call.
Sam Turner: I'll prototype the HMAC library and redis dedupe store. Also add a small integration test: fire concurrent requests that trigger fallback and assert quota service receives at most one final increment.
ops-bot: scheduled: canary rollout plan created (auth-decision-id -> 5% prod -> monitor 48h).
Ravi Singh: OK let's split tasks: Ezra + Sam implement headers & quota dedupe, Nora + Priya update console and billing pipeline for provisional flag, I (Ravi) will own rollout coordination and support comms.
Priya Rao: I'll draft a short blurb for customers explaining "pending attribution" behavior so they aren't surprised by transient spikes.
Nora Kim: one more internal API debate: should router ever override auth decision? Currently it can in rare capacity-fail cases. I'd argue it should never override silently; must emit a `compensate` event and require operator approval to flip historical attribution.
Ezra Gold: agree. Only operator or automated reconciliation should change committed attributions. Router may temporarily route traffic but mark events provisional rather than rewrite auth.
Ravi Singh: good call. Let's get PRs up today, target canary Monday. We'll reconvene after first 24h metrics.
